root-level module placement for an app that will later be a package
commit_reviews.summary: Clean greenfield websocket server scaffold with sound typing and structure, but its module-level singleton registry is hard to isolate.
Adds a clean channel-subscription feature that follows the existing registry/lock, message-dispatch, and HTTP-route patterns with proper cleanup and tests.

compounding_issues: Binary messages.db committed to git in session 3; every test run mutates it, so both timeout-recovery commits (e7a4f46, 5170302) contain only messages.db churn and zero code
Compiled __pycache__/*.pyc files committed from session 1 onward — the seed shipped no .gitignore, leaving persistent repo-hygiene debt

Session 3 integration scope (Redis backbone + cross-server routing + SQLite persistence) was too large for one session — 900s timeout produced two empty recovery commits and cross-server delivery was never validated

Duplicate persistence in multi-server deployments: origin saves via _publish_and_persist and every receiving server also saves in _deliver_from_redis (server.py:145), so distributed setups record duplicate rows
Story stopped at 3 of 5 planned sessions — the greenfield/feature_addition/integration arc never reached the intended continuation sessions
key_decisions: Session 1: websockets asyncio server + aiohttp HTTP sidecar (health/channels/messages REST endpoints) as the base architecture, with a substantial 191-line test suite
Session 2: channel-based subscription model layered on a thread-locked in-memory ClientRegistry keyed by client_id
Session 3: Redis pub/sub as the cross-server message backbone with server_id echo filtering (broker.py) plus an aiosqlite MessageStore for persistence
Broadcast path delivers locally-direct AND publishes to Redis for remote fan-out, using client→server/subscription keys in Redis for distributed routing
All modules (server/broker/store) instantiated as module-level singletons rather than injected dependencies
story_review.trajectory_description: Quality of implementation rose across the three substantive sessions: session 1 produced a clean single-server broadcaster, session 2 integrated channels cleanly with a large test expansion (+179 test lines), and session 3 added a coherent broker/store split. Test coverage and code volume grew steadily (17 tests, 370 test lines, 590 code lines, 0.63 ratio, all green at the end). However the run degraded in two ways: session 3 hit the 900s timeout and its two recovery commits contributed no code, and repository hygiene worsened monotonically as binary (.pyc, .db) artifacts accumulated in commits from session 1 onward.
story_review.summary: A coherent but unfinished story — the three real sessions formed a logical greenfield→channels→Redis-integration arc with healthy test growth, yet it stalled at 3 of 5 sessions on a session-3 timeout whose recovery commits contained only binary churn.
